name: accent marks
title: Spanish Accent Marks Practice: When to Write a Tilde, with a Quiz
description: Practice Spanish accent marks: stress rules, words ending in a vowel, n or s, question words, tú vs tu, sí vs si and accents on verbs, with 10 checked sentences.
answer: Spanish writes an accent mark when a word breaks the stress rules. Words ending in a vowel, n or s are naturally stressed on the second-to-last syllable (casa, hablan); words ending in another consonant are stressed on the last (papel, ciudad). If the stress falls elsewhere, write the accent: café, lápiz, música. Accents also separate pairs like tú and tu, sí and si.

rulesCaption: When Spanish words take an accent mark

rules.use: Stress on the last syllable, ending in vowel, n or s
Stress on the second-to-last, ending in another consonant
Stress three syllables from the end or earlier

rules.example: tú / tu, él / el, sí / si, mí / mi, sé / se, más / mas

rules.use: Weak vowel stressed next to a strong one

quiz.why: Ends in a vowel, stress on the second-to-last: no accent.
Stress three from the end: always an accent.
Ends in z, stress on the second-to-last: accent.
The pronoun you is tú, with accent.
Yes is sí, with accent; si means if.
The noun is fábrica (stress three from the end); fabrica is the verb.
Preterite él: viajó, stress on the last syllable, ending in a vowel.
The stressed i next to a: país, accent breaks the diphthong.
After a preposition, the pronoun is mí, with accent.

mistakes: Writing accents on every long word: «exámen» should be «examen» (ends in n, stress on the second-to-last), but the plural is «exámenes».
Dropping accents that change meaning: «hablo» (I speak) and «habló» (he spoke) are different verbs.
Confusing tu and tú, el and él, mi and mí: the stressed pronoun takes the accent.
Forgetting accents in indirect questions: «no sé dónde vive», «pregunta qué hora es».
Accenting one-syllable words without a pair: fue, dio, vio and ti never take an accent.

heritage: Heritage speakers often know where the stress falls but were never taught to write accents. Start with the high-frequency cases: preterite forms (habló, comió), question words (qué, cómo), and pairs like tú and tu. Reading your text aloud while checking each stressed syllable fixes most errors.
teacher: Dictate ten words and have students mark only the stressed syllable first. Then they decide with the table which ones need a written accent and compare with a partner.

faq.question: How do I know if a Spanish word needs an accent?
faq.answer: Find the stressed syllable. If the word ends in a vowel, n or s and the stress is on the last syllable (canción), it needs an accent. If it ends in another consonant and the stress is on the second-to-last (árbol), it needs one. Stress three syllables from the end always needs one (sábado).

faq.question: Why do some words lose or gain an accent in the plural?
faq.answer: Adding a syllable can move the word into another rule: canción → canciones loses it, examen → exámenes gains it. The stress stays on the same vowel; only the rule changes.

faq.question: Do capital letters need accents?
faq.answer: Yes. The Real Academia Española says capitals keep their accents: Álvaro, ÉXITO. Leaving them out is a typing habit, not a rule.
